newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia gives A$3.5 million food aid to Pyongyan.
newsitem.headline: Australia gives A$3.5 million food aid to Pyongyan.

text.p: Australia on Wednesday announced a A$3.5 million (US$2.6 million) food aid package for North Korea, as the secretive Stalinist state slides further toward famine after two years of severe floods that have devastated crops.
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said the aid would be channelled through the United Nations' World Food Programme, which has appealed for international help.

"This latest contribution from Australia comes at a time when it is clear that the food situation in North Korea is worsening, with millions of adults and children facing malnutrition and disease," Downer said in a statement.
Canberra has already given A$4 million in aid to Pyongyang.

The communist nation has been relying on international donations since flooding in 1995/96 left thousands without food. The United Nations said on Monday the situation was now worse, with crops devastated by the worst drought in 50 years.
